issue: Can a defendant challenge the substantive reasonableness of a sentence imposed under a Rule 11(c)(1)(C) plea agreement, such that the sentence is 'imposed in violation of law' and reviewable under 18 U.S.C. § 3742(a)(1)?

sides.position: Appellate jurisdiction exists under § 3742(a)(1) to review the substantive reasonableness of a sentence imposed under a Rule 11(c)(1)(C) agreement.
cases: United States v. Olson, 544 F. App'x 114, 117 n.1 (3d Cir. 2013)
United States v. Garcia, 522 F.3d 855, 860 (9th Cir. 2008)
United States v. Lovell, 811 F.3d 1061, 1063 (8th Cir. 2016)
United States v. Perez, 464 F. App'x 467, 469 (6th Cir. 2012) (resolving the challenge on waiver grounds without addressing jurisdiction)

sides.position: A sentence imposed pursuant to a Rule 11(c)(1)(C) agreement is not 'imposed in violation of law' because the defendant bargained for it, so there is no jurisdiction to review its reasonableness under § 3742(a)(1).
cases: United States v. Armendariz-Reza, 502 F. App'x 810, 812-13 (10th Cir. 2012)

quote: Our fellow circuits are divided on this question.
cite: United States v. Gonzalez, 62 F.4th 954 (5th Cir. 2023)
